cards.name: Turn before run
cards.summary: A large heading change from a standstill pivots in place first and only then hands over to the run cycle.
cards.behavior: Each update the character compares the heading requested by the pad with the heading it is currently committed to. When the gap exceeds 256 of the 4096 units that make a full turn, the character stays in the idle cycle and stores a pivot countdown of gap divided by 1024 plus one update, decrementing it while the direction is still held. Small gaps start the run cycle immediately. While the run plays, the loop aborts back to idle when the pad direction disappears for five updates or when the requested heading drifts more than 1048 units away from the committed one, and it aborts into the wall-press cycle after a three-update countdown while the contact flags say the body is pinned. The alert state also swaps the locomotion set: the aiming walk replaces the ordinary walk while an alert is active.

cards.name: Stance collision height
cards.summary: Every stance publishes its own body height and vertical probe, and a crouch is pushed back under a low ceiling.
cards.behavior: The character has three stances and each one carries its own collision numbers. Standing uses a 1100-unit body height with a 750-unit probe above the current floor, a crouch uses 496 units with a 250-unit probe, and lying down uses 136 units with the same 250-unit probe. Both contact spheres of the control are 450 units in radius. The probe is added to the current floor level and published as the height the control tests when it decides which hazard zones the body has entered, so a standing character enters zones a crawling one does not. When the character is not standing but its measured body height is still 500 units or more, the height is forced down to the crouch value, which is the guard against a crouch pushing the body through a ceiling it just fitted under.

cards.name: Prone crawl and stand-up
cards.summary: Lying down turns walking into a low crawl that can also play in reverse, and rising is gated on headroom.
cards.behavior: Dropping into the lying stance swaps the locomotion set for the crawl cycle and pins the reach probe to 450 units while the body is flat. Holding the rear direction while dropping adds 2048 units, exactly half a turn, to the committed facing, and the crawl then uses its reversed cycle, which lets the character crawl backwards without turning the body around. The drop starts with the bidirectional contact check skipped, and the check is restored as soon as the measured body height falls below 250 units, so the pose change is not fought by the collision volume it is collapsing. Rising needs a fresh button press plus a headroom probe: a 1500-unit clearance is traced from a point behind the body, and the character only commits to the stand-up cycle when that trace is clear.

constants.unit: engine units, per update, rate unverified

cards.name: Gravity step and target height
cards.summary: Vertical motion is a fixed gravity step with a ground snap, and the height reported to hit detection is clamped.
cards.behavior: The vertical component of the character's step loses 32 units every update, which is the gravity term, and it is zeroed as soon as it points downward while the control already reports ground contact, so the character rests on the floor instead of accelerating into it. The step is then handed to the shared control, which snaps the character onto the nearest floor level it reports. The same update republishes the vertical extent of the player's hit target, clamping it between 500 and 700 units so the body reads as one predictable volume whether the character is standing, crouched or falling.

cards.name: First-person aim entry
cards.summary: The aim view flips the camera to first person, stretches the aim probe and hides the third-person mesh over a short countdown.
cards.behavior: Entering the aim view sets the camera work's first-person flag and pads the aim probe to 460 units, a little longer than the 450 the exit path restores. It then arms a mesh counter at -6: while the counter is negative the third-person mesh is hidden as soon as the counter reaches zero, so the swap takes six updates and nothing pops. Leaving the view arms the same counter at +6 and the mesh becomes visible again when it returns to zero, at which point the menu lock is released. The entry rewrites three slots of the pitch table the pad handler reads, putting 320 in the first slot and 980 in the two outer slots, so the aim view can travel much further down than the default table allows.

cards.name: Three-hit melee combo
cards.summary: Two mirrored punches and a heavier finisher, each opening a 3D hit box in front of the body and gated by a line trace.
cards.behavior: The combo is a single motion with three strike windows at 4, 11 and 22 updates into the action. Each strike builds a power box in the body's local space, rotates it into world space and traces a hazard line from a rig joint to the box centre, so a strike that would pass through a wall is dropped instead of hitting something on the far side. The first two strikes are mirrored: a 200-unit lateral offset either side, a 600-unit reach, a box 400 wide, 200 tall and 400 deep, a constant 50-unit impulse and one faintness point. The third is central and heavier: 500 wide, 250 tall and 500 deep, a 100-unit impulse and three faintness points, which is what makes it the finisher. On the opening update the character also snaps its heading toward the nearest homing target within 2000 units and inside 1024 units of the current heading, and derives the pitch from the height difference, so the swing tracks a target standing above or below.

cards.name: Grab and choke chain
cards.summary: A grab opens a choke that can be pumped, dragged or released, with the held body shrunk so it stays inside the hold.
cards.behavior: The grab probes a capture box centred on the body, 501 units of half extent horizontally and 600 vertically, and only commits when the line from the character to the target centre is clear. A successful grab shrinks the target's lateral half size to 150 units so it cannot slip out of the hold. The choke then expires after 90 updates, ends when the target is released, and also ends if the choke button is let go for 9 consecutive updates. Pressing the button again from the re-choke state drains one faintness point and increments a chain counter; at 10 the character switches to the finishing animation. Releasing the target restores its original lateral half size.

cards.name: Damage, health and rations
cards.summary: Health is reconciled against pending damage every update, with armour mitigation, automatic ration use and invulnerability windows.
cards.behavior: Incoming hits land on the player's hit target and are folded into one health value each update: the pending damage is subtracted, the result is clamped to the maximum and floored at zero, and if health reaches zero while a ration is carried and the difficulty allows it, the ration is consumed automatically and health is restored inside the same update. A ration restores 256 points on normal and harder settings and 384 on easy, while the easiest setting restores the full maximum. The body armour halves the damage of the hits flagged for it before reconciliation. Recovering from a flinch or a knockdown grants 32 invulnerable updates, and a knockdown that leaves the body under 500 units tall drops the character into the lying stance rather than rebuilding a standing one.

cards.name: Guard vision cone
cards.summary: A guard tests the player against a horizontal cone, a vertical window and a line-of-sight trace before reporting a sighting.
cards.behavior: Sight is not computed by every guard on every update; a modulo of the global frame counter staggers the work so each guard recomputes on its own slot. A recompute measures the horizontal vector to the player, so distance and heading come from the ground plane, then the vertical gap between the two body positions. The player must be inside the guard's sight range, which is its eye length plus a 2000-unit allowance, and inside the same 2000 units of height. Within the range the player must either be closer than 500 units, in which case the cone is skipped entirely, or lie within 0x200 of a 4096-unit turn to either side of the guard's facing. Even then the guard needs a clear hazard trace back to the player and no other obstacle target in between; if any of those tests fail the guard records that it cannot see the player this update.

cards.name: Noise reach
cards.summary: Noise events carry a power code that decides which guards hear them and from how far.
cards.behavior: A guard ignores noise entirely while its noise power is zero. A power of 5 reaches guards within 1500 units of the noise origin, a power of 200 reaches the configured noise radius, which defaults to 0x1F40 units, and a power of 255 skips the distance test entirely and reaches any guard whose map masks overlap the maps the event carries. A power of 100 is a single-guard ping: only the guard whose index matches the sender reacts, and the event is cleared so no other guard can consume it. Distance is a full 3D comparison of positions, so a noise directly above or below a guard is still heard, and map ownership is checked before distance so a guard on an unrelated map never reacts. A heard noise sets the guard's noise flag, which the think routines translate into a look-around state.

cards.name: Alert escalation
cards.summary: Per-guard alert values drive a three-stage commander machine that raises and clears the global alert.
cards.behavior: Every guard keeps its own alert value. A confirmed sighting adds one per update, a partial look subtracts one, and losing the player subtracts a decay rate that defaults to 4. The commander folds those values into a stage machine of its own. In the calm stage the stage-0 eye length is used, and the moment any guard reaches 255 the global alert goes active, the stage advances and the alert counters reset. In the active stage the per-guard maximum is capped at 0x100 and the middle eye length is used; when the value falls to zero the alert drops to evasion, the stage advances again and a 300-update countdown starts. In the evasion stage that countdown runs down to calm, but any guard reaching 255 inside it re-raises the alert immediately. A commander-wide floor keeps an individual guard from decaying below the highest value the pack has reached, and the commander's own value only drops by 4 per update, so the alert bleeds out over many updates rather than snapping off.

cards.name: Chase camera follow
cards.summary: The follow blend runs a short exponential phase and then a linear countdown before the camera locks to the character anchor.
cards.behavior: When the follow flag is set the camera eases toward the character's camera anchor. For the first six updates it uses an exponential ease on position, rotation and pull-back distance; from there it switches to a linear blend counted down as 12 minus the elapsed updates, so the whole handover settles in 12 updates and then the flags are cleared and the camera is driven directly by the anchor. In both phases the pull-back distance eases toward 1000 units and the look target is rebuilt as the camera rotation direction scaled by that distance and added to the camera position, which is what keeps the framing tied to the anchor instead of to the body. A new camera system starts with a 320 zoom and a 10000-unit pull-back, so a freshly created camera begins far away and is drawn in by the blend.

cards.name: Body stepping and floor resolution
cards.summary: The shared control sweeps a step against map segments, pushes out of nearby walls, then resolves the vertical against floor and ceiling levels.
cards.behavior: Every control in the game integrates the same way. The step is added to the position and, when the combined horizontal step is larger than half the contact radius, swept against hazard segments; a hit projects the step back out to the surface, stores the touched segments and records a touch count for the owner to read. A second proximity pass collects segments within 500 units and pushes the position out along their reaction vectors, halving the remaining step to the contact radius when no reaction vector is produced. The vertical pass reads the floor and ceiling levels around the new position: when both exist and the ceiling sits less than 200 units above the previous floor level, the ceiling is discarded and the upper level is used as the floor instead, which is how shallow steps stop behaving like walls. The position is then snapped onto the higher floor or below the lower ceiling, the grounded flag records which of the two happened, and a missing ceiling is stored as 32000 so nothing clamps from above.

cards.name: Sidearm laser sight
cards.summary: The beam is traced along the aim axis and drawn as 1024-unit segments up to the traced distance.
cards.behavior: The sight defines a two-point segment in the weapon joint's local space that spans 10240 units along the aim axis, converts both ends to world space and clips the segment first against the map's hazard geometry and then against obstacle targets; the resulting length is what the renderer draws. The beam is built from 1024-unit segments, so the segment count is the length rounded up over 1024 and capped at 10, and when nothing is hit the length defaults to 10240 units, extended by 515 more in the first-person view. A traced length of 816 units or more is shortened by 815 so the visible beam stops just short of the surface instead of ending inside it. The first drawn vertex sits at a 300-unit offset in first person and at a negative offset in the third-person view.

cards.name: Item pickup volume
cards.summary: Placed items are only takeable inside a shallow box around the player, and they blink out shortly before they expire.
cards.behavior: An item can be taken only when it shares a map with the player and sits inside a box around the player position: 500 units on each horizontal axis and 1000 units vertically. On pickup the item, weapon or ammunition count is raised and clamped to the carried limit; a full inventory or a weapon that has not been unlocked shows a refusal message and leaves the pickup in the world. An item authored with a finite lifetime starts blinking once fewer than 90 updates remain, alternating between visible and hidden on an 8-update cycle with two updates hidden, and it destroys itself when the counter reaches zero. An item authored to last forever never blinks and never expires.

cards.name: Door threshold volume
cards.summary: A door tests whether the player stands inside a shallow box at its threshold before it closes or re-opens.
cards.behavior: The door builds its threshold box from its own half-width parameter, which defaults to zero and is raised to a 250-unit floor, plus a 50-unit margin on each side. The horizontal test compares the player position against the door centre on both ground axes, and the vertical test accepts only players standing between the door's own height and 2500 units above it, so a player on a walkway over the door is not treated as being in the way. The result runs every update while the door is closing: when the player is inside the volume the close is cancelled and the leaf re-opens, which is what stops a door shutting on the player. Leaf travel itself is eased toward a target offset at a default speed of 100 units per update.
